positions.name: MeridianGateEnactment
positions.frame: what is being settled as the gate's requirement, its environmental scope, and its ownership — read as one enacted rule rather than separate assertions?
positions.why: Conviction reads all four in the 'decision' region — 'now requires', the bolded Gate line, the Scope line, and the Owner line are each performed as settled/ratified rather than argued for, in contrast to src-2 which conviction reads as a supporting 'claim'. Relational and power reads reinforce this as one authority-ranking, legitimate-authority act spanning declaration (src-1/src-3), scope (src-4), and ownership (src-5) — the same enactment stated first in formal prose (src-1, register: formal) and then recapitulated in compressed technical-header shorthand (src-3/src-4/src-5, register: CompressedGateSpec/matter-of-fact). The set holds a register tension — formal narrative sentence vs. flat protocol bullets — without resolving it; both are the same rule being enacted.
